documents.title: User stories — CI, runners and platform (PLATFORM)
documents.body:
# User stories — CI, runners and platform (PLATFORM)

## Personas

- **The delivery session** — claims one issue, pushes one lane branch, runs the acceptance command locally, delivers one PR.
- **The reviewer and second approver** — reads the issue's Definition of Ready, the PR's evidence and the CI verdict; the builder never certifies its own gate.
- **The programme office** — keeps the unit protocol, the issue content contract, the two-run CI budget and the rework queue.
- **The release manager** — needs the deployed revision distinguishable from a green PR.
- **The public reader** — reads the standards, the design pack and the reworked projects on the design site.
- **The CI operator** — owns `ci-public.yml`, the runner pool and the run-time instrument.

## Stories

- As a delivery session, I want the unit claimed by a pushed lane branch before the first commit, so that no two sessions build the same thing.
- As a reviewer, I want exactly one PR per issue carrying `Closes #<n>`, its Definition of Ready and its evidence, so that the merge is a decision on facts.
- As a delivery session, I want a public CI mirror that runs the archetype's gates — fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, nextest, doctests and cargo audit — so that a green verdict means what it says.
- As the CI operator, I want every run to record its queue wait and wall time, so that the plan's speed budgets are measured, not inferred.
- As the programme office, I want each tranche-0 project reworked by the book and verified by an executable manifest, so that a standing row is green on evidence.
- As the public reader, I want the Delivery documents and the design pack published, so that the platform's claims are inspectable.

## Scenarios

- Given one issue, when a session starts, then the lane branch `issue/<n>-<slug>` is pushed before the work and the issue's Definition of Ready holds.
- Given the public repository, when CI runs, then no private `uses:` caller exists and `ci-public.yml` carries the rust-library gate set; the private archetype cannot be called from a public repo (#17 P1).
- Given a completed run, when it ends, then its queue wait and wall time are written to the job summary (#17 P4.1).
- Given a run at the final head, when it completes, then every job concludes inside its declared timeout (#17 P3.1).
- Given the PLATFORM row, when `verify-project.py` runs against a fresh snapshot, then the standing-row gate discharges with zero failures.
- Given the tranche-0 rework, when the conformance audit runs strict, then PLATFORM carries no P0/P1 finding.

## Verify

- `python3 scripts/verify-project.py --project PLATFORM --snapshot retained-snapshot/81e9ec6d653cd8d337d4c82aee693afb7a78405e` — the nine-check standing-row gate: charter, baselines, PI cadence, WSJF, demo credits, product findings, artefact standard, rework resolution, gate.
- `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --self-test` — the conformance contract holds.
- `python3 scripts/check-output-standard.py` — the Delivery class carries its required headings.
- `node docs/design/scripts/check-data.cjs` — the design pack's derived data is consistent.
- `gh run view` on the run recorded on #17 — every job inside its timeout, and the job summary carrying queue wait and wall time.

## Links

- Plan: `docs/plans/development-process-speed.md` sections 1 to 4 and "Acceptance targets".
- Units: #16 (queue sweep, open), #17 (public CI truth, closed), #526 (programme rework, closed).
- Record: `acceptance/programme/PLATFORM.toml`; `docs/evidence/rework/PLATFORM.json`; `docs/evidence/rework/PLATFORM.md`.

## Notes

Reconstructed from the delivered record on 2026-11-28 for the standard v4 Delivery set. The tranche-0 evidence is the issue evidence tables and the acceptance manifest; this document is the Delivery narrative, not a new claim.

documents.title: Acceptance criteria — CI, runners and platform (PLATFORM)
documents.body:
# Acceptance criteria — CI, runners and platform (PLATFORM)

## Scenarios

- The public mirror is canonical: no `ci.yml` exists at main, and `ci-public.yml` runs fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, nextest, doctests and cargo audit (#17 P1 and P2).
- A run at the final head concludes every job inside its declared timeout — `checks-shard` declares 120 minutes, the image job 60 minutes (#17 P3.1).
- Every completed run records its queue wait (`run_started_at - created_at`) and wall time in the job summary (#17 P4.1).
- A cancelled run is classified from its job timeline as superseded, timed out or evicted (#17 P3.3).
- One issue is one branch and one PR carrying `Closes #<n>`; the PR opens only after the acceptance command is green locally; the CI budget is two runs per issue.
- A documentation-only change runs the cheap checks and the final gate still verifies every applicable check (plan section 1.3).
- The PLATFORM row discharges its declared gate on a fresh snapshot: approved charter, three approved baselines, a PI cadence and refinement row for tranche 0, five WBS nodes carrying the four WSJF inputs, demo credits on accepted deliverables, no open P0 product finding, no due mandatory artefact, no unresolved P0/P1 package (`acceptance/programme/PLATFORM.toml`).
- The strict conformance audit carries no P0/P1 entry for PLATFORM.
- The tranche-0 rework publishes each project's Delivery set to the design site.

## Verify commands

- `gh run view 42680838271 --json jobs,event` — the audit's measured run; timeouts and cancellation classification read from the job timeline.
- `git grep -n 'cargo fmt\|cargo clippy\|cargo nextest\|cargo audit' origin/main -- .github/workflows/ci-public.yml` — the rust-library gate parity.
- `python3 scripts/verify-project.py --project PLATFORM --snapshot retained-snapshot/81e9ec6d653cd8d337d4c82aee693afb7a78405e` — the standing-row gate.
- `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --strict` — no P0/P1 entry for PLATFORM.
- `python3 scripts/check-output-standard.py` — the Delivery headings.
- `node docs/design/scripts/check-data.cjs` — the design pack's data is consistent.

## Results

- **Met.** The public mirror is canonical and gate parity is recorded (#17 P1 and P2 at `83f774c3`). The suite verdict lands inside its ceilings: shard 1 19m33s and shard 2 12m40s against 120 minutes, image 14m42s against 60 minutes. Queue wait and wall time are recorded: `created_at = run_started_at = 18:35:16Z`, 0 s queue, about 19m56s at the checks job, written to the job summary. The standing row is green: nine checks, zero failures, verdict `green` at snapshot `81e9ec6d`, generated 2026-11-26. #17 and #526 are closed.
- **Not met or not evidenced at tranche 0.** The plan's heavy-queue p95 under two minutes, warm full validation under fifteen minutes and docs-only feedback under two minutes have no recorded measurement; shard 1's 19m33s is the best measured full-suite figure. sccache hit rates, Cargo and Docker cache persistence, one disposable Postgres 18 per job and nextest bounded concurrency are proposed pilots with no recorded acceptance.
- **Superseded.** The plan's local commit-hook budget was rewritten by the 2026-11-20 owner direction: local Rust compilation is retired, and the compile/lint verdict is the GitHub-hosted `preflight.yml`.

## Status

met for the tranche-0 scope — the CI truth, the unit protocol and the rework instrument are delivered and green. The plan's remaining speed targets are open, continuing platform work carried by the live registry; they are not waived, and #16 remains open.

## Links

- Plan: `docs/plans/development-process-speed.md` "Findings", sections 1 to 4, "Acceptance targets".
- #17 evidence table at `83f774c3`; `docs/evidence/rework/PLATFORM.json`; `acceptance/programme/PLATFORM.toml`.

documents.title: Definition of ready — CI, runners and platform (PLATFORM)
documents.body:
# Definition of ready — CI, runners and platform (PLATFORM)

## Independent

The units are file-disjoint. #17 changes only `.github/workflows/ci-public.yml` and records its evidence on the issue; #16 reconciles issue state, branches and the sweep evidence with no product code; #526's batches are parts of one issue landing serially on `issue/526-u5a`. PLATFORM is a programme-level unit with no incoming blocker, and it sits outside the delivery dependency chain of the delivery projects.

## Negotiable

The outcome is fixed — a trustworthy CI verdict and a reworked, evidenced platform record. The mechanism was settled at delivery: #17's amendment of 2026-11-24 replaced the impossible private-workflow caller with the self-contained public mirror, a recorded scope move with its reason in the file header, not a silent one.

## Valuable

PLATFORM removes the gap the 2026-11-10 audit measured: a 40-run snapshot with 25 cancellations, 13 failures and zero successes, and a 102.2-minute run whose 75.1 minutes were queue. It maps to B1 — auditable decisions — because the unit protocol, the two-run CI budget and the acceptance manifest turn each delivery into dated, re-runnable evidence.

## Estimable

Every unit names its baseline SHA, its files and its verify command before work: #17 at `origin/main@a8c22f8e`, measured 2026-11-24; #526 at `main@7314a2d0`; the PLATFORM manifest at snapshot `81e9ec6d`. The plan's "Acceptance targets" give the measured budgets.

## Small

One issue is one branch and one PR; slices are commits on that branch. #17 is bounded by its own Definition of Done — no conveyor product code — and the repository's CI budget is two runs per issue. The 27 PLATFORM issues are separate units, not one batch.

## Testable

Every part carries a Given/When/Then scenario with a `Verify:`, and completion evidence is a command, result and SHA table, as #17's. The project-level test is executable: `acceptance/programme/PLATFORM.toml` discharged by `scripts/verify-project.py`, green at nine checks and zero failures on snapshot `81e9ec6d`.

## Dependencies

| Relation | Unit | Why | State at source |
|---|---|---|---|
| blocked-by | none | PLATFORM is a programme-level unit; `depends_on` is empty | measured 2026-11-24 |
| blocks | #22 | #17 P3 gates the merge-run tree-equality workflow change | open at #17's table, 2026-11-24 |
| related | #16 | the train run is the historical green baseline | open |
| related | #1 | the delivery protocol whose runs are the evidence | open |
| related | #8 | the deploy gate consumes the same archetype | open at #17's table |
| external | gitops-production | the private archetype is the gate source; its changes belong to its own queue | private repository, consumed by mirror |

## Notes

Reconstructed for the standard v4 Delivery set on 2026-11-28; the project's active state and its open residuals are the record's, not this document's.

documents.title: Definition of done — CI, runners and platform (PLATFORM)
documents.body:
# Definition of done — CI, runners and platform (PLATFORM)

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Verify |
|---|---|
| The public mirror is canonical and gate-parity with the archetype's rust-library set | `git grep -n 'cargo fmt\|cargo clippy\|cargo nextest\|cargo audit' origin/main -- .github/workflows/ci-public.yml`; no `ci.yml` at main (#17 P1 and P2) |
| A run at the final head concludes inside its declared timeouts | `gh run view` on the 2026-11-24 run recorded on #17 — shard 1 19m33s, shard 2 12m40s against 120 minutes, image 14m42s against 60 minutes |
| Every completed run records queue wait and wall time | the checks job's job summary — 18:35:16Z, queue 0 s, wall about 19m56s at `83f774c3` |
| A cancelled run is classified from its job timeline | `gh run view` with the jobs and event fields (#17 P3.3) |
| PLATFORM's declared gate discharges on a fresh snapshot | `python3 scripts/verify-project.py --project PLATFORM --snapshot retained-snapshot/81e9ec6d653cd8d337d4c82aee693afb7a78405e` — green, nine checks, zero failures |
| No P0/P1 conformance entry for PLATFORM | `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --strict` |
| The Delivery documents carry the standard's required headings | `python3 scripts/check-output-standard.py` |

## Evidence at completion

#17 carries a full evidence row per part at `83f774c3`: P1.1 the absent `ci.yml`, P2.1 the five gates, P3.1 the times inside the ceilings, P4.1 the queue-wait instrument. #526 is closed; tranche 0 was closed and reviewed 2026-11-17, and the rework instrument is re-runnable — `governance/conformance.json`, `audit-programme-conformance.py` with `--strict` and `--self-test`, `programme-record.py`, `verify-project.py` with `acceptance/programme/PLATFORM.toml`. Under the 2026-11-27 scope change, #526 lands tranches 0 to 5 and the tranche-6 governance, with the tranche-6 member packs and tranches 7 to 13 continuing in #838 and its successors. PLATFORM's record: `docs/evidence/rework/PLATFORM.json` green at nine checks and zero failures, generated 2026-11-26; the note of 2026-11-21 green at six checks at `d7293f96`. #16 remains open; this document does not claim the queue sweep complete.

## Repo gate

The PR's CI is `ci-public.yml`: `checks-shard` runs fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, nextest, doctests and cargo audit, and the image job builds beside it. `issue-dor.yml` refuses an unready issue, and repository guards deny a PR unless the head is `issue/<n>-*` and the body carries `Closes #<n>`, failing open only on an unparseable command. Since the 2026-11-20 owner direction local Rust compilation is retired: the git hooks run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1` and actionlint on changed workflows; the compile/lint verdict is the GitHub-hosted `preflight.yml`, and `cargo-guard.py` on m4 is for interactive work only. Commits are signed off for DCO; the CI budget is two runs per issue.

## Merge and closure

Each issue closes through its one PR on `issue/<n>-<slug>`; slices are commits and never get their own PR. The merge queue is the single integration gate, and a squash merge is verified by its merge commit and an empty tree diff before the branch is deleted. Closure evidence follows the #302 gate. PLATFORM itself does not close: the standing row's gate reads "The standing platform row carries an approved charter and a baseline; it does not close."

## Links

- Plan: `docs/plans/development-process-speed.md`; `docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` issue content contract.
- Units: #16 (open), #17 (closed), #526 (closed), #838 (successor).
- Record: `acceptance/programme/PLATFORM.toml`; `docs/evidence/rework/PLATFORM.json`.

documents.title: Closure review — CI, runners and platform (PLATFORM)
documents.body:
# Closure review — CI, runners and platform (PLATFORM)

## Outcome vs acceptance

The tranche-0 scope is delivered on the closed units #17 and #526 and on the platform row's own rework, with #16 open:

- **The public CI truth.** `ci-public.yml` is the canonical public mirror; the impossibility of calling the private archetype from a public repository is recorded in its header, and the mirror runs the archetype's rust-library gates. A run at the final head produced a verdict inside its declared ceilings, with queue wait and wall time on the run (#17 at `83f774c3`).
- **The rework.** The tranche-0 projects were reworked by the reconstituted lifecycle, and the instrument is re-runnable: `governance/conformance.json`, `audit-programme-conformance.py --strict --self-test`, `programme-record.py`, `verify-project.py` with `acceptance/programme/PLATFORM.toml` (#526, closed).
- **The platform row.** Green on nine executable checks with zero failures, verdict `green` at snapshot `81e9ec6d` (2026-11-26): approved charter, three approved baselines, the PI cadence and refinement rows for tranche 0, five WBS nodes with the four WSJF inputs, demo credits, no open P0 product finding, no unresolved P0/P1 package.

Against the plan's acceptance targets, queue wait and wall time are recorded and the suite fits its ceiling. The p95 heavy-runner queue under two minutes, warm full validation under fifteen minutes and docs-only feedback under two minutes are not evidenced; shard 1 measured 19m33s.

## Evidence

- #17's completion table at `83f774c3`, one row per part; #17 closed.
- #526 closed. Tranche 0 was closed and reviewed 2026-11-17; under the 2026-11-27 scope change #526 lands tranches 0 to 5 and the tranche-6 governance, and the tranche-6 member packs and tranches 7 to 13 continue in #838 and its successors.
- `docs/evidence/rework/PLATFORM.json` — green, nine checks, zero failures at snapshot `81e9ec6d`, generated 2026-11-26.
- `docs/evidence/rework/PLATFORM.md` — the 2026-11-21 note, green at six checks at `d7293f96`.
- `acceptance/programme/PLATFORM.toml` — the manifest those checks discharge, and the repository's `scripts/verify-project.py` as the runner.

## Open items

1. #16, the queue sweep and merged-branch cleanup, is still open; its evidence document `docs/evidence/2026-11-12-delivery-system.md` is the unit's record, and this review does not claim it complete.
2. The plan's speed budgets with no recorded measurement at tranche 0: heavy-runner queue p95 under two minutes, warm full validation under fifteen minutes (19m33s on shard 1 is the best measured), and docs-only PR feedback under two minutes.
3. The plan's pilots not evidenced as accepted: sccache hit rates, Cargo and Docker cache persistence, one disposable Postgres 18 per job with cross-process setup coordinated by a database advisory lock, nextest with bounded concurrency, and the section 1.3 always-running change classifier with its final gate.
4. The 2026-11-20 owner direction supersedes the plan's local-hook budget: no Rust compilation on local hardware; the compile verdict is the GitHub-hosted `preflight.yml`, and the non-compiling hooks remain only as fast local checks.
5. PLATFORM stays `active`; the programme's remaining tranches and the tranche-6 member packs continue in #838 and its successors and may return platform changes to this row.

## Decision

The tranche-0 review accepts the delivered scope, and this closure review records its decision: PLATFORM is a standing row and does not close. The gate's own words are "The standing platform row carries an approved charter and a baseline; it does not close." The open items above are carried by the live registry and the continuing lane; they are named here, not waived, and none is reported as complete.

## Links

- Plan: `docs/plans/development-process-speed.md`.
- Units: #16 (open), #17 (closed), #526 (closed), #838 (successor).
- Record: `acceptance/programme/PLATFORM.toml`; `docs/evidence/rework/PLATFORM.json`; `docs/evidence/rework/PLATFORM.md`; programme registry key `PLATFORM`.
